title: Elastic IP Addresses and Network Interfaces
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of elastic ip addresses and network interfaces and its relationship to AWS Networking and Amazon VPC.
Interpret the example and identify at least one prerequisite or boundary relevant to elastic ip addresses and network interfaces.
Propose a safe verification or troubleshooting step and record one security, reliability or cost consideration.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn elastic ip addresses and network interfaces in the context of AWS Networking and Amazon VPC. You will connect the listed subtopics to a practical decision, inspect a small example, and define evidence that would confirm or disprove your assumptions.
content.why_it_matters: Elastic IP Addresses and Network Interfaces matters because it is one part of amazon vpc and network reachability. Real workloads depend on explicit prerequisites, correct permissions, predictable behavior and a way to verify outcomes. Learning the decision points helps you distinguish a working demonstration from a safe and supportable design.

content_blocks.title: VPC routing and network controls
content_blocks.alt_text: Reachability combines subnet routing, a route target, addressability, security groups, network ACLs and service-specific controls.
content_blocks.caption: A route alone does not prove reachability; all relevant network and identity controls matter.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
**Core idea.** Elastic IP Addresses and Network Interfaces belongs to AWS Networking and Amazon VPC. VPC reachability is an end-to-end result of address ranges, subnet associations, routes, gateways, security groups, network ACLs and service endpoints—not just one firewall rule.

The PDF lists these subtopics: Elastic IP concepts; Elastic network interfaces; IP address assignment; Address management and cost awareness. Treat them as a connected workflow rather than a list to memorize. Start with the workload requirement, identify the AWS resource/control involved, and write down who owns configuration and operation.

content_blocks.title: Practical reasoning
content_blocks.text: **Apply it safely.** For elastic ip addresses and network interfaces, name the prerequisites and the expected result before making a change. Prefer a read-only inspection or local/static example first. Then plan a normal case, a failure case, and a verification step. In a live account, require the account owner-approved sandbox, narrow permissions, spend visibility and cleanup plan. Do not put credentials in code or commit local configuration files.

items.title: Elastic IP concepts
items.text: Identify the AWS resource or design decision involved, the permissions and prerequisites it needs, and the evidence that shows it is configured as intended.

items.title: Elastic network interfaces
items.text: Trace the path from source to destination through address ranges, routing, gateways and filtering controls. Verify both forward and return paths; one successful configuration screen is not proof of reachability.

items.title: IP address assignment
items.text: Trace the path from source to destination through address ranges, routing, gateways and filtering controls. Verify both forward and return paths; one successful configuration screen is not proof of reachability.

items.title: Address management and cost awareness
items.text: Estimate the complete workload, including requests, storage, data transfer and dependent services. Compare the estimate with actual usage and alerts; an alert is not a hard spend cap.

content_blocks.title: Inspect route tables: Elastic IP Addresses and Network Interfaces
content_blocks.code:
# Read-only example related to: Elastic IP Addresses and Network Interfaces
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --query "RouteTables[].[RouteTableId,VpcId,Associations[0].SubnetId]" --output json
content_blocks.expected_output: JSON metadata for route tables; reachability still depends on complete routes and filtering controls.

content_blocks.text: Use least privilege, keep Block Public Access/private defaults unless a justified reviewed requirement says otherwise, and document cost/cleanup before live changes.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one successful example as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: The example may not test permissions, regional/service prerequisites, retries, recovery, quotas or edge cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Write acceptance criteria, test a failure path, inspect logs/state and record the limits of the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Changing a live resource before confirming its effect and cost.
common_mistakes.why: Cloud changes can expose data, break traffic or leave billable dependencies behind.
common_mistakes.fix: Start read-only, use an approved sandbox, review the change, tag ownership and verify cleanup.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying broad permissions or credentials into source files.
common_mistakes.why: Broad permissions and leaked long-lived credentials increase the impact of mistakes.
common_mistakes.fix: Use scoped roles/temporary credentials, keep secrets in approved stores and review access boundaries.
